## Setting up the parser

The parser reads one line at a time and keeps a small amount of state between lines, so a long file never sits in memory at once.

It has two parts: a tokenizer that splits the input, and a reducer that folds the tokens into the result. Each can be tested on its own.

- the tokenizer never allocates per character
- the reducer is pure, so a failing line can be replayed in a test without the rest of the file
- both report the line number on errors

```ts
export function parse(line: string, state: State): State {
  const tokens = tokenize(line);
  return tokens.reduce(step, state);
}
```
